title: Alice in Wonderland
author: d'après Lewis Carroll
desc: Alice suit un lapin blanc pressé… et tombe dans un monde complètement fou.

p: Alice was sitting by the river with her sister. She was bored. Her sister's book had no pictures. "What is the use of a book without pictures?" she thought.
Suddenly, a White Rabbit ran past her. He had a waistcoat and a watch. "Oh dear! Oh dear! I'm late!" he said.
Alice had never seen a rabbit with a watch! She followed him across the field and jumped into a big rabbit hole.
She fell down, down, down. It was a very long fall. She passed cupboards and bookshelves on the walls. Finally, she landed on a pile of leaves.
She was in a long hall with many doors. All the doors were locked. On a small glass table, there was a tiny golden key, and a bottle. On the bottle, a label said: *DRINK ME.*
Alice drank. She became very small, as small as a mouse! Now she could go through the little door. But oh no, the key was on the table, and she was too small to reach it!
Then she found a little cake. It said: *EAT ME.* She ate it, and she grew, and grew, until her head touched the ceiling!
Alice started to cry. Her big tears made a lake on the floor. Then she found a fan and became small again… and fell into her own lake of tears!
She swam to the shore with a mouse, a duck, a dodo and other strange animals. "This is the strangest day of my life," said Alice.
Alice walked through the woods. A big Cheshire Cat smiled at her from a tree. Its smile was very wide.
"Which way should I go?" asked Alice.
"That depends where you want to go," said the Cat. "But everyone here is mad. I'm mad. You're mad."
"How do you know I'm mad?"
"You must be. Or you wouldn't be here." And the Cat disappeared, slowly, until only its smile was left.
Then Alice found a strange tea party. The Mad Hatter, the March Hare and a sleepy Dormouse sat at a long table. It was always six o'clock, so it was always tea time.
"Why is a raven like a writing desk?" asked the Hatter.
Alice thought hard. "I don't know. What's the answer?"
"I haven't the slightest idea," said the Hatter.
At last, Alice arrived in a beautiful garden. Gardeners shaped like playing cards were painting white roses red.
Then the Queen of Hearts arrived. She was very angry, all the time. "Off with her head! Off with his head!" she shouted at everybody.
There was a trial. Somebody had stolen the Queen's tarts. Alice was called as a witness. But she was growing bigger again.
"Off with her head!" screamed the Queen.
"Who cares about you?" said Alice. "You're nothing but a pack of cards!"
All the cards flew into the air and fell on her. Alice screamed… and opened her eyes.
She was by the river, with her head on her sister's knees. A few leaves had fallen on her face. It was all a dream. A wonderful, crazy dream.
